A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same AnimeGamer study and contain readable main text, equations, Tables 1–3, Figures 1–9, and Appendices A–F. The bibliography is relocated in v2; no substantive material is missing.

before.justification: v1 reports original benchmark comparisons, a human evaluation with 20 participants, and ablation results in Tables 1–3 and Figures 5–7.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark comparisons, human evaluation, and ablation results, including their supporting appendix details.

M1.justification: The animation-shot encoder and decoder, MLLM next-state prediction, training losses, decoder adaptation, and sliding-window inference remain unchanged in Section 3 and Appendices A and C.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same anime-film training collection, WebVid pretraining samples, and evaluation benchmark covering 20 characters, 940 movements, and 133 environments. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: GC, GFC, and GSC remain the evaluated comparators in Tables 1–2, while Figure 5 retains GC and GFC. Their definitions and the ablation comparator set are unchanged.

E3.justification: The benchmark construction, evaluation metrics, training schedules, ablation 8:2 split, and human-evaluation design are identical, including the protocols documented in Appendices C–E.

E4.justification: Both versions retain the same encoder variants, warm-up and motion-scope ablations, cosine-loss comparison, and decoder-adaptation ablation. Table 3 and Figures 5–8 contain the same analyses and examples.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The human-ranking conversion and averaging procedure in Appendix E is unchanged.

E6.justification: All numerical entries in Tables 1–3 and the qualitative examples are unchanged. For example, AnimeGamer retains CLIP-I 0.8132 in Table 1 and GPT-4V overall score 8.36 in Table 2.

T1.justification: The task formulation, representation definitions, motion-scope construction, and Equations 1–4 are unchanged. Neither version adds formal assumptions, theorems, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims concerning infinite anime life simulation, action-aware representations, contextual consistency, dynamic animation, and comparative effectiveness.

C2.justification: The explanations of contextual consistency, motion control, and decoder adaptation are unchanged. Section 5 retains the closed-domain limitation and identifies generalization to unseen characters as future work.

D1.justification: Appendices A–E retain the same special tokens, preprocessing instructions, prompts, model configurations, LoRA settings, learning rates, and training steps. Code, checkpoint, and project access information is also unchanged.

R1.justification: The same 86 bibliography entries and research-positioning discussion are retained. Bibliographic differences are limited to updated citation-backlink page numbers following appendix relocation.

P1.justification: v2 places the bibliography after Appendix F instead of between the conclusion and appendices. The main-text and appendix wording is unchanged; the arXiv version/date stamp is updated.

P2.justification: Moving the bibliography changes reference-page text flow, leaves most of page 9 blank, and shifts the appendix pages. Figures 1–9 and Tables 1–3 retain their content, captions, and visual design.

improvement.justification: v2 preserves the scientific content, empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information of v1. Relocating the bibliography changes document navigation and whitespace but provides no meaningful overall quality gain or loss.
